html:
SMTO-GWT-0038 — SMTO can't safely send sign-in details through this computer yet

GUID: c3a38a59-76f2-4bb0-ac48-83ddb2f67613
Slug: gateway-credential-route-untrusted
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • Before SMTO hands a computer any sign-in details for a website or service, it checks that the connection to that computer is trusted and ready. That check failed, so SMTO stopped before asking for or sending those details.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the computer used for this request and select Check connection. It should show Connected. SMTO only passes sign-in details over a connection it has just confirmed.
  2. If the check fails, make sure that computer is on, connected to the network and its Gateway program is running, then check again. This error often means SMTO simply couldn't reach the Gateway when it checked.
  3. If the computer shows an Identity changed badge in the Gateways list, have the person who manages it confirm it is the right computer before you continue. SMTO won't send private details to a computer whose identity it can't trust.
  4. When it shows Connected, ask SMTO again to make the web request. If an earlier request in the same Task went through, check its result first. This check stopped before sending, but other steps in the Task may already have run.

What success looks like

  • The computer shows Connected, and the web request either runs or asks you for sign-in details.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't turn off security checks or switch the connection to an unsecured one to make it work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Before collecting API credentials for an HTTP request, the selected Gateway route was not ready: its HTTPS route had no configured TLS trust record, or the /capabilities readiness check failed or could not be completed; this alone does not identify a certificate defect.

What this means

  • The selected HTTPS route lacked its configured trust record, or the public capability readiness check raised an exception before credentials could be requested. This does not by itself identify a certificate defect. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The selected HTTPS route lacked its configured trust record, or the public capability readiness check raised an exception before credentials could be requested. This does not by itself identify a certificate defect.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing TLS route configuration from a failed capability query using the retained producer and readiness facts.

How to fix it

  • Restore the selected Gateway route: run Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways, confirm the Gateway is reachable, its TLS identity is trusted (tls_trust_state, and the HTTPS base URL has a configured route record) and its /capabilities response returns the same node with http_runtime.ready true and the http_request capability tag. Then send the HTTP request again; GatewayClient.http_readiness and SelectedRouteOpener.open fail this way before any credential is requested.
  • Restore the selected route and verify Gateway identity and HTTP capability readiness through supported controls before supplying credentials.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended route passes identity and capability readiness checks before receiving private values.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
